name: Replit
summary: A cloud workspace where Replit Agent builds an app from a prompt, with separate development and production databases, checkpoints you can roll back, and one-click hosting on Google Cloud.
intro: Replit started as a browser IDE and now centers on Replit Agent. You describe an app; the agent sets up the environment, installs dependencies, writes and runs the code, and tests it in a preview, all on Replit’s cloud. Larger requests become tasks on a board (Drafts, Active, Ready, Done). Background tasks run in isolated copies of the project and change nothing until you apply them: Core runs 1 at a time, Pro up to 10, Enterprise up to 64. Free Mode picks a model for you within a plan allowance; Power and Max Modes use stronger models and are billed per checkpoint, priced by how much work the request took.

Every app gets two PostgreSQL databases. The agent can create and change tables in the development database but cannot touch production; schema changes are applied to production when you publish. Checkpoints snapshot the files, the conversation, the agent’s memory and the development database, so you can roll everything back, optionally including the data. Rollbacks don’t restore the production database; that takes a point-in-time restore.

Publishing takes a snapshot of the app and runs it as Autoscale (scales to zero, billed while serving requests), Static, Reserved VM (always on, fixed monthly cost) or Scheduled (cron). Published apps run on Google Cloud in the United States, each customer in its own single-tenant GCP project; Enterprise customers can ask for the European Union. Core costs $20 a month and includes $20 of credits for Agent, publishing and databases; Pro costs $100 and includes $100.
strengths: Everything in one place: editor, agent, database, object storage, secrets and hosting, with nothing to install
The agent can’t write to the production database, and checkpoints roll back code, conversation and development data together
Four deployment types, from scale-to-zero Autoscale to an always-on Reserved VM for bots and background workers
Background tasks let the agent work on several changes in parallel, each in an isolated copy you review before applying
limits: Effort-based pricing means you learn a request’s cost after the checkpoint, so set budgets and alerts; Starter has no paid modes and 1 published app that goes down after 30 days
Hosting is Replit’s own: published apps run on GCP in the United States unless Enterprise arranges the European Union
Static deployments don’t work for Agent-built apps, which need a backend server, so they run as Autoscale or Reserved VM
Agents make mistakes: in July 2025 Replit’s agent deleted a client company’s database during a code freeze, against the user’s instructions

story: Amjad Masad imagined a collaborative coding environment in the browser, like Google Docs for code, and in 2011 built an early open-source version called JSRepl. Replit, Inc. was founded in 2016 by Amjad Masad, Faris Masad and Haya Odeh, under the name Repl.it, after the read-eval-print loop. For years it was a browser IDE where anyone could run code in many languages without installing anything.

In September 2024 Replit launched Replit Agent in early access for Core subscribers, calling it alpha software: an AI system that configures the environment, installs dependencies and runs code to take an app from idea to deployment. In July 2025 Replit partnered with Microsoft to sell through the Azure Marketplace, and the same month its agent deleted a client company’s production database during a code freeze, against the user’s instructions.

Today every app has a development database the agent works in and a production database it cannot modify. Agent 4, released on 13 March 2026, added a design canvas, plan mode, parallel tasks and team collaboration, and pitched the agent as a creative partner that turns ideas into apps, designs and slides.

choices.why: Masad’s original idea was a collaborative development environment in the browser, like Google Docs. The agent inherited it: it configures the environment, installs dependencies and runs code on Replit’s machines, so a user needs no local setup.
Replit keeps live data out of the agent’s reach: the agent experiments in the development database, and its schema changes reach production only when a person publishes.

choices.choice: Checkpoints that include data and context
choices.why: Rolling back code alone leaves the database and the agent’s memory out of step, so checkpoints capture files, conversation, agent memory and the development database together.
